note: Full transcript of the real Claude + Grok requirements panel run of 2026-11-09: both drafts, both reviews, the merge and its rationale, and the gate verdicts. Synthetic practice data; no patient data.
brief: On CO-50 medical-necessity denials, the specialist must not mark the appeal packet ready unless a clinical-note reference and a filing-deadline date are both present.

proposalA.problem: Denial specialists at Northwind Imaging can currently mark a CO-50 medical-necessity appeal packet ready even when the packet has no clinical-note reference and no filing-deadline date. CO-50's only allowed next action is to appeal with the coverage policy and a clinical-note reference, and timely filing in this demo is 90 days from the date of service, so a packet missing either element is not actually appealable. The workbench needs a readiness gate that blocks the ready action on CO-50 lines until a clinical-note reference (a DOC-### id) and a filing-deadline date are both present, and that tells the specialist exactly what is missing.
users: Denial specialist — works appealable denials and is the only role that marks a CO-50 packet ready; cannot override the gate in v1
PFS lead — sees counts by CARC class and appeal-ready volume; does not mark packets ready
Biller — resubmits corrected claims (CO-16, CO-4) and must keep that path unchanged
Coder — owns modifiers and diagnosis pointers; this product suggests no CPT or ICD changes
Front desk — reads eligibility only and does not work denials
inScope: A readiness gate on CO-50 denial lines requiring both a clinical-note reference and a filing-deadline date
Disabling the 'mark appeal packet ready' action and naming each missing item on the button label
Validating the clinical-note reference as a non-empty DOC-### identifier
Computing and displaying the filing deadline as date of service plus 90 days, and treating a blank deadline as missing
Enforcing the denied -> appeal-ready state transition only after the gate passes
Showing the CO-50 meaning and the only allowed next action verbatim on the denial detail screen
Keeping CO-16, CO-4, CO-197, PR-1 and OA-23 handling on their current paths
Workqueue display of deadline risk bands and sort by days remaining for CO-50 work
outOfScope: Any override, supervisor approval, or force-ready path (deferred past v1)
Deciding medical necessity, recommending or changing a diagnosis code
Storing or rendering clinical note bodies, attachments, or document content
Real payer portals, clearinghouse routes, plan ids, or actual claim submission
Writing off balances, adjusting patient responsibility, or editing PR-1 and OA-23 lines
Appeal letter authoring, coverage-policy text management, and appeal outcome tracking (upheld/overturned)
Changing the CO-16 / CO-197 / CO-4 workflows or their next actions
Any HIPAA determination or business associate agreement; the PHI scanner is a demo scanner

assumptions.text: The readiness gate applies to CO-50 denial lines only. CO-16 and CO-197 keep their current path, and no other CARC code gains a gate.

Nobody may override the gate in v1 — not the denial specialist, not the PFS lead. The ready action stays disabled until both fields are present; there is no override control and no justification-to-proceed path.
A clinical-note reference is a non-empty DOC-### identifier. The field holds an identifier, not a document body; whitespace-only or non-conforming values count as missing.
The filing deadline is the date of service plus 90 days. A blank deadline (the remit did not carry one and none is derivable) fails the gate.
When blocked, the specialist sees the missing items named on the ready button itself, so the then-clause of each acceptance criterion is directly observable.

requirements.statement: On a CO-50 denial line, the appeal packet readiness gate must pass only when a clinical-note reference and a filing-deadline date are both present; otherwise the 'mark appeal packet ready' action is disabled.
requirements.rationale: CO-50's only allowed next action is to appeal with the coverage policy and a clinical-note reference, and an appeal without a filing deadline cannot be worked against timely filing (pack/carc-demo.md, pack/payer-northwind.md).

requirements.statement: While the gate fails, the ready action's label must name each missing item ('clinical-note reference', 'filing deadline', or both), and the appeal checklist must show each gate item as present or missing.
requirements.rationale: Q-5: the specialist must see what is blocking them without guessing, and the detail pattern requires the ready action to name each missing item (pack/patterns/detail-checklist.md).

requirements.statement: No role may override the readiness gate in v1. The product exposes no override, force-ready, or approval-to-proceed control, and the denied -> appeal-ready transition is refused for any caller while the gate fails.
requirements.rationale: Q-2 and pack/roles.md: the denial specialist cannot override the gate in v1, and the PFS lead does not mark packets ready.

requirements.statement: The clinical-note reference field accepts a non-empty identifier shaped DOC-###. Empty, whitespace-only, or non-conforming values are treated as missing by the gate, and no note body is stored or displayed.
requirements.rationale: Q-3 and pack/phi-policy.md: allowed identifiers are PAT-###, CLM-###, DOC-###, and the field is an identifier rather than clinical content.

requirements.statement: The filing-deadline date for a CO-50 line is the date of service plus 90 days. The denial detail and workqueue show that date and its risk band against the demo clock of 17 November 2026; a blank deadline is reported as missing and fails the gate.
requirements.rationale: Q-4 and pack/payer-northwind.md: timely filing is 90 days from date of service and a blank deadline is treated as missing.

requirements.statement: CO-16, CO-4, CO-197, PR-1 and OA-23 lines keep their current path. The readiness gate is not applied to them, and their next actions are unchanged.
requirements.rationale: Q-1 scopes the gate to CO-50 only; pack/claim-states.md keeps PR-1 and OA-23 out of the denied/appeal path entirely.

requirements.statement: The CO-50 denial detail screen shows the claim lines, the CARC meaning from the demo table, and the only allowed next action copied verbatim, with no diagnosis-change suggestion anywhere on the screen.
requirements.rationale: pack/patterns/detail-checklist.md and pack/carc-demo.md: this product does not decide medical necessity and must not invent or alter a next action.

requirements.statement: The claim state machine permits appeal-ready for a CO-50 line only after the readiness gate passes; the gate is evaluated by one shared domain rule that the UI calls rather than reimplements.
requirements.rationale: pack/claim-states.md states appeal-ready is allowed for a CO-50 line only after the gate passes; pack/patterns/detail-checklist.md requires the component to call the domain rule.

requirements.statement: The denial workqueue lists appealable denials in a dense table sorted by days remaining to the filing deadline, shows the deadline risk band and gate status without opening the row, filters by CARC class, and groups patient-responsibility lines separately.
requirements.rationale: pack/patterns/workqueue.md defines the pattern, and the specialist needs to see which CO-50 packets are blocked before their deadlines run out.

requirements.statement: Every identifier rendered or stored by the feature is synthetic and shaped PAT-###, CLM-###, or DOC-###; intake briefs, diffs, and seed data are scanned for SSN, email, phone, raw MRN, and date-of-birth patterns, and a hit blocks the run before a requirement document is written.
requirements.rationale: pack/phi-policy.md defines the allowed identifiers and the blocking demo scanner.

openQuestions.text: When the date of service is present but the remit carried no deadline, should the product compute date of service plus 90 days automatically and treat the gate item as present, or still require the specialist to confirm the computed date?

If the computed filing deadline is already overdue against the demo clock, should the gate still pass on a present-but-overdue date, or should overdue be surfaced as a separate warning on the ready action?
Where does the DOC-### clinical-note reference come from — free entry by the specialist, or selection from a seeded list of document ids? Is any existence check performed on the id?
How does the gate behave when one claim carries multiple CO-50 lines: is the packet per line or per claim, and must every CO-50 line satisfy the gate before the packet is ready?
Does the coverage policy named in the CO-50 next action need its own checklist item in a later version, and would it join the gate or stay advisory?
Should blocked gate attempts be recorded in an audit trail for the PFS lead, and if so what is captured beyond the claim id and the missing item names?

Can a packet already in appeal-ready be reopened if the clinical-note reference is later cleared, and does it return to denied?

The workbench must not decide medical necessity, must not change a diagnosis to clear coverage, and must fail closed in v1 with no override. A button-only disable is not enough: a forced ready transition must also be rejected. A blank or non-matching deadline must not look safe on the queue.

assumptions.text: CO-50 only. CO-16 and CO-197 keep their current path.
Nobody in v1. The ready action stays disabled until both fields are present.

requirements.statement: The new readiness gate applies only to CO-50 denial lines. CO-16 keeps its current path: Correct the missing element named by the remark and resubmit the claim. CO-197 keeps its current path: Attach the authorization reference if one exists. Otherwise route to the authorization desk for a retro request. On a mixed claim, the gate must not pull a non-CO-50 line into the appeal.
requirements.rationale: A class-wide gate would block billers on submission errors and could turn patient responsibility into a false appeal. pack/carc-demo.md and pack/claim-states.md limit appeal-ready to a CO-50 line after the gate passes.

requirements.statement: The denial specialist must not mark a CO-50 appeal packet ready unless both a clinical-note reference and a filing-deadline date are present. If either is absent, the line stays out of appeal-ready.
requirements.rationale: CO-50's only allowed next action is: Appeal with the coverage policy and a clinical-note reference. Do not change the diagnosis code in this product. Sending the packet without the note reference, or without a deadline, is the failure this gate exists to stop.

requirements.statement: Nobody may override the gate in v1. The ready action stays disabled until both fields are present. No role gets an override control.
requirements.rationale: pack/roles.md bars the denial specialist from overriding the gate in v1. An override would let a packet leave with a missing note or a missing timely-filing date.

requirements.statement: A clinical-note reference counts only when it is a non-empty identifier shaped DOC-###. Empty text, whitespace, free text, and a document body do not count. The field stores the identifier, not the note.
requirements.rationale: pack/phi-policy.md allows DOC-### only. Pasting a note body into the identifier invites disallowed personal data into the demo and does not prove a note was referenced.

requirements.statement: The filing deadline that satisfies the gate is the date of service plus 90 days, per Northwind Health timely filing. A blank deadline fails the gate. A date that is not equal to the date of service plus 90 days does not satisfy the gate. The specialist cannot type a substitute date to clear the gate.
requirements.rationale: pack/payer-northwind.md sets timely filing at 90 days from the date of service and treats a blank remit deadline as missing. Accepting a mistyped or mismatched date would show a false filing window and could miss the payer clock.

requirements.statement: When the gate blocks, the ready control names each missing item using the phrases clinical-note reference and filing deadline. It names only items that are actually missing. It does not name a coverage-policy reference as a missing gate item in v1. When both items are present and valid, the control is enabled and named Mark appeal packet ready.
requirements.rationale: pack/patterns/detail-checklist.md requires the ready action to name each missing item. Q-5 requires that the then-clause be observable. Naming an item the gate does not check would train specialists to satisfy the wrong checklist.

requirements.statement: The ready action calls the domain readiness rule and does not reimplement that rule in the component. A ready transition attempted while either gate item is missing is rejected, the line does not become appeal-ready, and the rejection names the missing items.
requirements.rationale: pack/patterns/detail-checklist.md says the ready action calls the domain rule. A disabled button alone can be bypassed, which is the compliance failure mode of a UI-only gate.

requirements.statement: The detail view shows the demo-table meaning and the only allowed next action for the line's code, and it must not invent a meaning. For CO-50 the meaning is: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a medical necessity by the payer. The only allowed next action is: Appeal with the coverage policy and a clinical-note reference. Do not change the diagnosis code in this product. The product does not decide medical necessity, does not change a diagnosis code, does not invent a modifier, and does not write off a balance. PR-1 next action is: Post the amount to patient responsibility. Do not open an appeal. OA-23 next action is: Confirm the prior payer adjudication. Do not work this as a denial. CO-4 next action is: Correct the modifier and resubmit. Do not invent a modifier in this product. An unknown code stays unmapped.
requirements.rationale: pack/carc-demo.md forbids invented meanings and forbids this product from deciding medical necessity or recommending a different diagnosis. pack/roles.md forbids write-off and diagnosis changes. Those escapes would otherwise sit next to a blocked appeal.

requirements.statement: appeal-ready is allowed for a CO-50 line only after the readiness gate passes. A blocked line remains denied. The gate does not skip the line to appeal-submitted.
requirements.rationale: pack/claim-states.md allows appeal-ready for a CO-50 line only after the gate passes. Marking ready is not payer submission; this demo has no portal or clearinghouse route (pack/payer-northwind.md).

requirements.statement: The workqueue is a dense table of appealable denials with a separate patient-responsibility group. It sorts by days remaining to the filing deadline and can be filtered by CARC class. Deadline risk is visible without opening the row. Using the demo clock of 17 November 2026, risk is overdue when days remaining are negative, urgent within 14 days, soon within 45 days, and otherwise comfortable. A blank deadline is labelled missing and is not labelled comfortable, and blank-deadline rows sort ahead of dated rows so they are not buried.
requirements.rationale: pack/patterns/workqueue.md and pack/payer-northwind.md make timely-filing risk the queue's safety signal. A blank deadline labelled comfortable is how an untimely CO-50 appeal gets ignored.

requirements.statement: Only the denial specialist may mark a CO-50 packet ready, and only when the gate passes. Front desk, coder, biller, and PFS lead have no ready action and no override. PFS lead can see counts by CARC class. Front desk does not work denials.
requirements.rationale: pack/roles.md separates denial work from billing, coding, front desk, and PFS lead oversight. A lead override or a biller ready action would bypass the specialist gate.

requirements.statement: Patients, claims, and documents in the workbench use only synthetic identifiers shaped PAT-###, CLM-###, and DOC-###. The workbench must not display or store a disallowed personal-identifier shape listed in pack/phi-policy.md. This demo scanner is not a HIPAA determination and the project does not offer a business associate agreement.
requirements.rationale: pack/phi-policy.md blocks runs that contain disallowed personal-identifier shapes before a requirement document is written. The booth product must not become a place those shapes are shown.

openQuestions.text: v1 fails the gate when the remit date differs from date of service plus 90 days. Should the detail screen also show the raw remit date beside the calculated date, and should any later version treat the remit date as authoritative?
Should an overdue deadline that otherwise equals date of service plus 90 days block ready, or only show overdue risk? v1 does not block on overdue alone.
Must DOC-### resolve to a stored synthetic document before the gate passes, or is a well-formed non-empty identifier enough? v1 checks shape and non-emptiness only.
What digit length, letter case, and internal spacing are allowed for DOC-### beyond the three-digit examples used here?
If one claim has multiple CO-50 lines, must every line pass the gate before any line can become appeal-ready?
CO-50's next action also says to appeal with the coverage policy. Should a coverage-policy reference become a third gate field? v1 does not gate on it and must not label it as a missing gate item.
Who may record the DOC-### value, and is an audit trail required when ready is attempted, blocked, or completed?
Are the urgent and soon bands inclusive of day 14 and day 45, is a deadline on the demo clock day urgent or overdue, and which timezone applies to 17 November 2026?
If the clinical-note reference or the filing deadline is cleared after the line is appeal-ready, must the line leave appeal-ready?

Before any production use, who confirms the demo CARC meanings and fixture remark pairings against the current X12 external code list? This demo must leave an unknown code unmapped and must not invent a meaning.

critiqueOfA.author: B
strengths: Q-1 through Q-5 are recorded as assumptions, and the gate stays on CO-50 only with no v1 override and a disabled ready action until both fields are present.
CARC next actions are copied verbatim in carcReferences and in AC-13, AC-14, and AC-15, with no invented meanings and no diagnosis-change path.
The clinical-note reference is a non-empty DOC-### identifier, no note body is stored, and fixtures stay on PAT-###, CLM-###, and DOC-###.
Most P0 gate failures have scenarios, the ready label names each missing item, and a direct ready request is refused while the gate fails.
Rationales cite the pack paths for the 90-day filing rule, claim states, roles, and the shared domain-rule pattern.

defects.point: AC-11 and SCN-3 require risk band 'urgent' for filing deadline 2026-12-04 against the demo clock of 17 November 2026, and justify it as within 14 days. That interval is 17 days. pack/payer-northwind.md sets urgent to within 14 days and soon to within 45 days, so the observable band is 'soon'. A P0 then-clause that is false would fail a correct implementation.

OQ-1 reopens whether a present date of service and a remit with no deadline should auto-compute date of service plus 90 days and satisfy the gate. Q-4, the assumptions entry, inScope, REQ-5, and AC-11 already fix the deadline as date of service plus 90 days and fail only a blank deadline. The same gate input cannot be both required and undecided, so the filing-deadline half of the gate is not stably testable.

REQ-6 says CO-4 and OA-23 keep their current paths, but no acceptance criterion asserts CO-4's next action 'Correct the modifier and resubmit. Do not invent a modifier in this product.' or OA-23's next action 'Confirm the prior payer adjudication. Do not work this as a denial.' AC-13 and AC-14 cover only CO-16, CO-197, and PR-1.

AC-17's then-clause (detail and workqueue must not restate the field checks locally) cannot be checked by an observer; it needs source inspection. SCN-4 lists P0 AC-2 but uses CLM-120 rather than CLM-108 and never observes the empty clinical-note reference before overwriting it, so AC-2 is not exercised. SCR-3 lists SCN-9, which is a pre-document scanner step and does not use that screen.

adopt: Q-1 through Q-5 assumption records and the CO-50-only gate with no v1 override
Verbatim CARC next actions in carcReferences, AC-13, AC-14, and AC-15
DOC-### identifier rule with no note body, and synthetic PAT/CLM/DOC fixtures
AC-8 refusal of a direct ready request while the gate fails, and button labels that name each missing item
reject: AC-11 and SCN-3 expected risk band 'urgent' for 2026-12-04
OQ-1, which re-decides the Q-4 filing-deadline rule already required by REQ-5
AC-2 coverage claim on SCN-4 and the SCR-3 to SCN-9 screen link
AC-17 as an observer-checkable acceptance criterion

attributes.note: Fixtures stay inside PAT-###, CLM-###, and DOC-###, with no SSN, email, phone, raw MRN, date of birth, or real name. No role can override the gate, a bypass ready request is refused, and the product does not decide medical necessity or change a diagnosis code.

D-A1 sets the wrong deadline risk band for a 17-day interval, and D-A2 leaves the date-of-service-plus-90 rule both required and open, so a core gate outcome is not stable. D-A3 also leaves CO-4 and OA-23 path preservation untested.

D-A4: AC-17 is not observer-checkable, P0 AC-2 is cited by a scenario that does not execute it, and SCR-3 is tied to a scanner scenario that does not use the screen. Those breaks make the trace from requirement to check unreliable even though ids and the shared-rule intent are otherwise clear.

critiqueOfB.author: A
strengths: Every CARC reference quotes the next action verbatim from the table, and all six codes (CO-16, CO-50, CO-197, CO-4, PR-1, OA-23) plus the unmapped rule are covered by requirements and criteria, so no code is left dangling.

REQ-7/AC-16 close the UI-only-gate hole: a forced ready transition is rejected by the domain rule, not just by a disabled button, and the rejection names the same missing-item phrases an observer reads on the control. This matches pack/patterns/detail-checklist.md.

Traceability is complete: every requirement carries at least one acceptance criterion, and every P0 criterion is exercised by at least one named scenario (AC-1/SCN-6, AC-13/SCN-5, AC-24/SCN-11, AC-28/SCN-16, and so on), with three screens each tied to the scenarios they serve.

Deadline arithmetic and risk bands are correct against pack/payer-northwind.md and the 17 November 2026 demo clock (2026-08-20 + 90 = 2026-11-18; 2026-11-18 urgent, 2026-12-17 soon, 2027-01-18 comfortable, 2026-09-29 overdue), and REQ-10 refuses to label a blank deadline comfortable.

Identifier hygiene is clean throughout: only PAT-###, CLM-###, DOC-### appear, REQ-4 keeps a note body out of the identifier field, and REQ-12 repeats that the scanner is not a HIPAA determination and no BAA is offered.
Negative-authority coverage is strong: SCN-12 through SCN-15 prove PFS lead, front desk, coder, and biller have no ready action and no override, which is the v1 answer to Q-2.

defects.point: SCN-5 says the disabled control "names filing deadline as missing" for CLM-225, whose deadline field is populated with 2026-12-01. REQ-6 states the control "names only items that are actually missing." The two statements contradict each other, so an implementer cannot tell whether a present-but-mismatched date should be reported as missing or as mismatched, and AC-13 does not fix the wording. Define a distinct phrase (for example, filing deadline does not match date of service plus 90 days) or drop the mismatch branch.

REQ-5 and AC-13 add a gate condition the question round did not grant. Q-4 says the deadline is date of service plus 90 days and that a blank deadline fails; it does not say a populated date that differs must fail. pack/payer-northwind.md states the shown deadline is that date or blank, so the mismatch case is outside the fixture. Making equality a release-blocking P0 condition can hold a packet that has a usable deadline. OQ-1 flags the question but the requirement already decided it.

REQ-8 bundles four distinct rules (CARC meaning and next-action display for five codes, no medical-necessity or diagnosis decision, no invented modifier, no write-off, unmapped handling) and carries six criteria including AC-29 on write-off. Splitting the display rule from the prohibited-action rule would keep each criterion traceable to one statement.

SCN-13 (front desk) and SCN-14 (coder) start with "Open the denial workbench available to this role" and are both attached to SCR-1, the denial workqueue. pack/roles.md says front desk does not work denials, so the starting state is unclear about what screen these roles can reach at all. Name the concrete entry point or state that the route is absent, otherwise the expected result is not checkable.

AC-17 asks a reviewer to inspect "how missing items are determined" and confirm there is no "second copy of the presence checks." That is a code-review step, not something a product observer can check from the running demo. Phrase it as an artifact review with a named owner, or pair it with a behavioural check (same phrases from rule and button, already in AC-16).

adopt: REQ-7 with AC-16: enforce the gate in the domain rule and reject a forced ready transition, not only disable the button.
REQ-10's handling of a blank deadline: label it missing, never comfortable, and sort those rows ahead of dated rows so they are not buried.
OQ-6 plus the REQ-6 clause that a coverage-policy reference must not be named as a missing gate item in v1, which keeps the two-field gate honest while leaving the third field open.
The negative-authority scenario set (PFS lead, front desk, coder, biller all have no ready action and no override) as the test of the Q-2 answer.
AC-29's before-and-after write-off check attached to both the blocked and the appeal-ready state.
reject: REQ-5's date-equality condition as a P0 gate rule. Keep v1 at presence-or-blank per Q-4 and show the calculated 2026-11-18 as an advisory comparison, moving the equality question entirely into OQ-1.
SCN-5's wording that a populated, mismatched deadline is named "missing" on the control; it conflicts with REQ-6 and would mislead the specialist about what to fix.

attributes.note: Fails closed with no override for any role in v1, confines ready authority to the denial specialist with explicit negative checks for the other four roles, keeps CO-50 out of diagnosis and write-off territory, restricts identifiers to PAT-###/CLM-###/DOC-### with a criterion that no disallowed shape is displayed, and repeats that the demo scanner is not a HIPAA determination and no BAA is offered.

CARC text, role boundaries, state transitions, and the 90-day arithmetic are all faithful to the pack, but D-B1 leaves an internal contradiction between REQ-6 and SCN-5 over whether a present-but-mismatched deadline is reported as missing, and D-B2 turns an undecided mismatch rule into a release-blocking condition the question round never granted. D-B4 adds an unclear starting state for the front-desk and coder scenarios.

Ids follow the conventions, every requirement has a criterion, every P0 criterion lands in a scenario, three screens map to their scenarios, and ten open questions capture what is still undecided. D-B3 (an overloaded REQ-8) and D-B5 (a code-inspection criterion) are tidy-ups, not structural failures.

synthesis.problem: On a CO-50 medical-necessity denial, a Northwind Imaging denial specialist can today mark an appeal packet ready with no clinical-note reference and no filing-deadline date. CO-50's only allowed next action is to appeal with the coverage policy and a clinical-note reference, and Northwind Health timely filing in this demo is 90 days from the date of service, so a packet missing either element is not actually appealable and can silently miss the payer clock. The workbench needs a CO-50-only readiness gate that fails closed in v1: the ready action is disabled until both items are present, the disabled control names exactly what is missing, the rule lives in the domain layer so a forced transition is also rejected, and a blank deadline never looks safe on the queue. The product must not decide medical necessity, change a diagnosis code, invent a modifier, or write off a balance.
users: Denial specialist - works appealable denials and is the only role that may mark a CO-50 packet ready, and only when the gate passes; cannot override the gate in v1
Biller - resubmits corrected CO-16 and CO-4 claims and must not be blocked, redirected, or given a ready action by the CO-50 gate
PFS lead - sees counts by CARC class and the read-only ready-attempt audit log; has no ready action and no override
Coder - owns modifiers and diagnosis pointers; opens denial detail read-only, receives no CPT or ICD suggestion, and has no ready action
Front desk - reads eligibility only; the denial workqueue route is absent for this role
inScope: A readiness gate on CO-50 denial lines requiring both a non-empty DOC-### clinical-note reference and a filing-deadline date before the line may become appeal-ready
A ready control that is disabled while the gate fails and whose accessible name lists exactly the missing gate items
Enforcement of the gate in one shared domain rule that both the denial detail and the workqueue call, so a forced ready transition is rejected as well as the disabled button

Filing deadline computed as date of service plus 90 days, used for the gate and for the risk band; the remit deadline is used only when the date of service is absent; a mismatch between the two is an advisory, not a block
Per-line gating: the appeal packet is per CO-50 line, and each CO-50 line is gated independently
Verbatim display of the demo-table meaning and the only allowed next action for every code in the table, with unknown codes left unmapped

Workqueue sorted by days remaining with risk bands visible on a closed row, blank deadlines labelled missing and sorted ahead of dated rows, CARC class filter, and a separate patient-responsibility group
Role separation with explicit negative checks for front desk, coder, biller, and PFS lead
A read-only audit entry for every ready attempt, blocked or completed
Synthetic identifiers only, shaped PAT-###, CLM-###, and DOC-###, with the pre-run demo scanner blocking disallowed personal-identifier shapes
outOfScope: Any override, supervisor approval, or force-ready path in v1, including a PFS lead override; no override control is designed, built, or stubbed
Applying the readiness gate to CO-16, CO-197, CO-4, PR-1, or OA-23
Deciding medical necessity, recommending or changing a diagnosis code, suggesting CPT or ICD changes, inventing a modifier, or writing off a balance
Treating the coverage-policy citation as a third gate field in v1; it is an advisory checklist item only
Storing or rendering a clinical note body, attachment, or document content in the clinical-note reference field
Existence checks against a document store for DOC-### values in v1; the check is shape and non-emptiness only
Payer submission of any kind: real plan ids, portals, clearinghouse routes, and the appeal-submitted, upheld, and overturned transitions
Production X12 certification; the demo meanings and fixture remark pairings are confirmed against the current X12 external code list by the product owner before any production use
Any HIPAA determination or business associate agreement; the scanner is a demo scanner

assumptions.text: CO-50 only. CO-16 and CO-197 keep their current path, and no other CARC code gains a gate. On a mixed claim the gate is offered only on the CO-50 line.
Nobody in v1. The ready action stays disabled until both fields are present, and no role - specialist, biller, coder, front desk, or PFS lead - has an override control.
A non-empty DOC-### id. The field is an identifier, not a document body; whitespace-only, free text, and note bodies count as missing.
Date of service plus 90 days. A blank deadline fails the gate.
Name the missing items on the button. The then-clause can be observed from the control's accessible name.

requirements.statement: The readiness gate applies only to CO-50 denial lines. CO-16, CO-197, CO-4, PR-1, and OA-23 keep their current paths and are never gated. On a mixed claim, the gate is offered only on the CO-50 line and must not pull a non-CO-50 line into the appeal packet.
requirements.rationale: Q-1 scopes the gate to CO-50. pack/carc-demo.md gives each code one allowed next action and pack/claim-states.md limits appeal-ready to a CO-50 line, so a class-wide gate would block billers and could turn patient responsibility into a false appeal.

requirements.statement: A CO-50 appeal packet may be marked ready only when both a clinical-note reference and a filing-deadline date are present for that line. If either is absent the ready control is disabled and the line stays in denied. The packet is per CO-50 line; each CO-50 line on a claim is gated independently.
requirements.rationale: CO-50's only allowed next action is: Appeal with the coverage policy and a clinical-note reference. Do not change the diagnosis code in this product. An appeal without the note reference, or without a timely-filing date, is the failure this gate exists to stop (pack/carc-demo.md, pack/payer-northwind.md).

requirements.statement: Nobody may override the gate in v1. The product exposes no override, force-ready, or approve-anyway control to any role, and no justification-to-proceed path exists.
requirements.rationale: Q-2 and pack/roles.md: the denial specialist cannot override the gate in v1 and the PFS lead does not mark packets ready.

requirements.statement: A clinical-note reference counts only when it is a non-empty identifier shaped DOC- followed by exactly three digits in upper case, with no surrounding text. Empty, whitespace-only, free text, lower-case or wrong-length variants, and document bodies count as missing. The field stores and displays the identifier only. In v1 the specialist types the identifier and no existence check is made against a document store.
requirements.rationale: Q-3 and pack/phi-policy.md: allowed identifiers are PAT-###, CLM-###, and DOC-###, and pasting a note body into an identifier field invites disallowed personal data into the demo.

requirements.statement: The filing deadline for a CO-50 line is the date of service plus 90 days, computed by the product and used for both the gate and the risk band. When the date of service is absent, the deadline carried on the remit is used instead. When neither is available the deadline is blank, is labelled missing, and fails the gate. A deadline that is present but already overdue still satisfies the gate and is shown with the overdue risk band. When the remit carried a deadline that differs from the computed date, both dates are shown and the difference is an advisory note; it does not block the gate and no control lets a specialist type a substitute date.
requirements.rationale: Q-4 and pack/payer-northwind.md: timely filing is 90 days from the date of service and a blank deadline is treated as missing. The question round granted only presence-or-blank, so a mismatched-but-present date must not become a release-blocking gate condition.

requirements.statement: While the gate fails, the ready control is disabled and its accessible name is 'Mark appeal packet ready - missing: <items>', naming only the items that are actually missing, using the phrases 'clinical-note reference' and 'filing deadline'. It never shows a generic not-ready message and never names a coverage-policy reference as a missing gate item. When both items are present the control is enabled and named 'Mark appeal packet ready'.
requirements.rationale: Q-5 and pack/patterns/detail-checklist.md: the ready action names each missing item, and naming an item the gate does not check would train specialists to satisfy the wrong checklist.

requirements.statement: The readiness rule lives in one domain module. The denial detail control and the workqueue row call that module and do not reimplement the presence checks. A ready transition invoked on a CO-50 line while either gate item is missing is rejected by the domain rule, the line does not become appeal-ready, and the rejection names the same missing-item phrases an observer reads on the control.
requirements.rationale: pack/patterns/detail-checklist.md says the ready action calls the domain rule and does not reimplement it. A disabled button alone can be bypassed, which is the compliance failure mode of a UI-only gate.

requirements.statement: The denial detail shows the claim lines, the demo-table meaning, and the only allowed next action for the line's code, copied verbatim, plus the appeal checklist. For CO-50 the checklist shows the clinical-note reference and the filing deadline as gate items (present or missing) and the coverage-policy citation as an advisory, non-gating item. An unknown code stays unmapped with no invented meaning and no gate.
requirements.rationale: pack/patterns/detail-checklist.md defines the detail layout and pack/carc-demo.md forbids invented meanings and allows only one next action per code.

requirements.statement: The product offers no control that decides medical necessity, changes or suggests a diagnosis or procedure code, invents a modifier, or writes off a balance, in any state before or after the gate.
requirements.rationale: pack/carc-demo.md states this product does not decide medical necessity and does not recommend a different diagnosis; pack/roles.md bars write-offs and diagnosis changes for everyone in the demo.

requirements.statement: appeal-ready is reachable for a CO-50 line only after the readiness gate passes. A blocked line remains denied, and marking ready never skips the line to appeal-submitted. If a gate item is cleared after a line reaches appeal-ready, the line returns to denied and the ready control is disabled again with the missing item named.
requirements.rationale: pack/claim-states.md allows appeal-ready for a CO-50 line only after the gate passes, and this demo has no payer portal or clearinghouse route (pack/payer-northwind.md).

requirements.statement: The denial workqueue is a dense table of appealable denials with a separate patient-responsibility group, sorted ascending by days remaining to the filing deadline and filterable by CARC class. Against the demo clock of 17 November 2026 the risk band is overdue when days remaining are negative, urgent from 0 through 14 days inclusive, soon from 15 through 45 days inclusive, and comfortable above 45 days. A blank deadline is labelled missing, is never labelled comfortable, and sorts ahead of dated rows. Deadline risk and a blocked/ready marker are visible without opening the row.
requirements.rationale: pack/patterns/workqueue.md and pack/payer-northwind.md make timely-filing risk the queue's safety signal; a blank deadline labelled comfortable is how an untimely CO-50 appeal gets ignored.

requirements.statement: Only the denial specialist may mark a CO-50 packet ready, and only when the gate passes. The front desk has no denial workqueue route at all; the coder may open denial detail read-only from the coding queue; the biller works CO-16 and CO-4 resubmission only; the PFS lead sees counts by CARC class and the audit log. None of these roles has a ready action or an override.
requirements.rationale: pack/roles.md separates denial work from billing, coding, front desk, and PFS oversight, and states the specialist cannot override the gate in v1.

requirements.statement: Every ready attempt on a CO-50 line, blocked or completed, writes an audit entry holding the claim and line identifier, the acting role, the demo timestamp, the outcome, and the missing-item phrases when blocked. The audit log is read-only and visible to the PFS lead; it contains no override field.
requirements.rationale: Resolves the open audit question so the fail-closed gate is reviewable by oversight without giving oversight a way to clear a blocked packet (pack/roles.md).

requirements.statement: Every patient, claim, and document identifier shown or stored by this feature is synthetic and shaped PAT-###, CLM-###, or DOC-###. Intake briefs, diffs, and seed data are scanned before a requirement document is written for a social security number shaped ###-##-####, an email address, a phone number, a raw MRN followed by an identifier, and a date labelled as a date of birth; a hit blocks the run. The scanner is a demo scanner, not a HIPAA determination, and the project does not offer a business associate agreement.
requirements.rationale: pack/phi-policy.md defines the allowed identifiers, the blocking pre-run scanner, and the explicit limits of that scanner.

requirements.statement: The CARC meanings and fixture remark pairings shown in the product carry a visible provenance note stating that they are shortened demo text that the product owner must confirm against the current X12 external code list before any production use, and that an unknown code stays unmapped.
requirements.rationale: pack/carc-demo.md requires both lists to be confirmed against the current X12 external code list before production use and forbids inventing a meaning.

analystA.summary: 2 P0 · 2 P1 from critique · 1/3 attributes met
findings: D-A1 P0 OTHER: AC-11 and SCN-3 require risk band 'urgent' for filing deadline 2026-12-04 against the demo clock of 17 November 2026, and justify it as within 14 days. That interval is 17 days. pack/payer-northwind.md sets urgent to within 14 days and soon to within 45 days, so the observable band is 'soon'. A P0 then-clause that is false would fail a correct implementation.

D-A2 P0 UNTESTABLE: OQ-1 reopens whether a present date of service and a remit with no deadline should auto-compute date of service plus 90 days and satisfy the gate. Q-4, the assumptions entry, inScope, REQ-5, and AC-11 already fix the deadline as date of service plus 90 days and fail only a blank deadline. The same gate input cannot be both required and undecided, so the filing-deadline half of the gate is not stably testable.

D-A3 P1 MISSING_COVERAGE: REQ-6 says CO-4 and OA-23 keep their current paths, but no acceptance criterion asserts CO-4's next action 'Correct the modifier and resubmit. Do not invent a modifier in this product.' or OA-23's next action 'Confirm the prior payer adjudication. Do not work this as a denial.' AC-13 and AC-14 cover only CO-16, CO-197, and PR-1.

D-A4 P1 UNTESTABLE: AC-17's then-clause (detail and workqueue must not restate the field checks locally) cannot be checked by an observer; it needs source inspection. SCN-4 lists P0 AC-2 but uses CLM-120 rather than CLM-108 and never observes the empty clinical-note reference before overwriting it, so AC-2 is not exercised. analystB.summary: 1 P0 · 4 P1 from critique · 2/3 attributes met
findings: D-B1 P0 OTHER: SCN-5 says the disabled control "names filing deadline as missing" for CLM-225, whose deadline field is populated with 2026-12-01. REQ-6 states the control "names only items that are actually missing." The two statements contradict each other, so an implementer cannot tell whether a present-but-mismatched date should be reported as missing or as mismatched, and AC-13 does not fix the wording. Define a distinct phrase (for example, filing deadline does not match date of service plus 90 days) or drop the mismatch branch.

D-B2 P1 OTHER: REQ-5 and AC-13 add a gate condition the question round did not grant. Q-4 says the deadline is date of service plus 90 days and that a blank deadline fails; it does not say a populated date that differs must fail. pack/payer-northwind.md states the shown deadline is that date or blank, so the mismatch case is outside the fixture. Making equality a release-blocking P0 condition can hold a packet that has a usable deadline. OQ-1 flags the question but the requirement already decided it.

D-B3 P1 OTHER: REQ-8 bundles four distinct rules (CARC meaning and next-action display for five codes, no medical-necessity or diagnosis decision, no invented modifier, no write-off, unmapped handling) and carries six criteria including AC-29 on write-off. Splitting the display rule from the prohibited-action rule would keep each criterion traceable to one statement.

D-B4 P1 OTHER: SCN-13 (front desk) and SCN-14 (coder) start with "Open the denial workbench available to this role" and are both attached to SCR-1, the denial workqueue. pack/roles.md says front desk does not work denials, so the starting state is unclear about what screen these roles can reach at all. Name the concrete entry point or state that the route is absent, otherwise the expected result is not checkable.

D-B5 P1 OTHER: AC-17 asks a reviewer to inspect "how missing items are determined" and confirm there is no "second copy of the presence checks." That is a code-review step, not something a product observer can check from the running demo. Phrase it as an artifact review with a named owner, or pair it with a behavioural check (same phrases from rule and button, already in AC-16).
